newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: MEDIENOS PLAUSHAS TO ISSUE GDRS IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: MEDIENOS PLAUSHAS TO ISSUE GDRS IN JULY.

text.p: Lithuanian cardboard producer Medienos Plaushas said on Monday that it has agreed with the Bank of New York to convert around 30 percent of its current shares into global depository receipts (GDRs) in July.
"We agreed with the Bank of New York that part of our current shares will be issued as gross depository receipts in July," the company's director general, Petras Chesna, told Reuters.
"We will not issue new shares but intend to convert around 30 percent of our current shares into GDRs," Chesna added.
He also said that the number of shares to be converted might still change.
The company unveiled its plan to convert part of its shares into GDRs last month but did not indicate the possible time table when it might happen.
Chesna also said that the company completed the distribution of its eight million litas share issue.
"The whole eight million litas issue was subscribed to by the current shareholders and now the share capital of the company will stand at 28.1 million litas," Chesna said.
Medienos Plaushas is one of the three corporates listed on the elite official list of the Vilnius bourse.
The company holds around 40 percent of the corrugated cardboard market in the country and is the sole producer of egg containers in the Baltic region.
The company is 33 percent owned by investment company Invalda and around 14 percent of its stake is held by foreign investors, Estonia's Hansapank among them.
The company posted an audited net profit of 1.7 million litas in 1996 and 830,000 litas for the first quarter of 1997.
